predecessors.name: Unified Silla
predecessors.text: the centre and north of the peninsula that Kung Ye took from Silla and from the local lords: 'almost two-thirds of the land once controlled by Silla' (Gungye page)

successors.name: Goryeo
successors.text: the whole of Taebong, taken over in the coup of 918

ledger.x: 904: the kingdom is renamed Majin 'after a suggestion by Ajitae'.
905: the capital moves to Cheorwon ('Kung Ye moved the capital to Cheorwon' in 905).
c.905: Kung Ye holds 'almost two-thirds of the land once controlled by Silla', including Chungcheong; 'Myeongju and Paeseo local aristocrats submitted to him'.
911: the kingdom takes the name Taebong ('He changed the name of his kingdom to Taebong in 911').
918: four generals overthrow Kung Ye and enthrone Wang Kon, who restores the name Goryeo.

wars.name: Later Three Kingdoms (Taebong phase)
wars.outcome: Kung Ye took the centre and north from Silla; the state fell to its own generals in 918, not to a rival.

certainty.note: No frontier is dated or described on the pages; every border of the state is approximate.
